subject.title: [Feature]: Move away from useMultiFileAuthState for Baileys

question: Should WhatsApp auth use plugin-owned Kysely tables in `state/openclaw.sqlite`, or a dedicated SQLite database justified by auth-specific volume and lifecycle, and what rollback and legacy-file deletion guarantees must migration provide?
rationale: Repository policy establishes SQLite-first, single-owner persistence, but source evidence cannot determine the intended database boundary, retention period, rollback behavior, or acceptable handling of duplicated credential material without maintainer intent.

options.title: Shared database schema
options.body: Add WhatsApp-owned Kysely tables to `state/openclaw.sqlite`, migrate transactionally, verify reopen, and remove legacy files only after a bounded backup period.

options.title: Dedicated WhatsApp database
options.body: Use a dedicated SQLite database only if measured auth volume, schema isolation, backup, or lifecycle requirements do not fit the shared state database.

options.title: Retain multi-file state
options.body: Continue atomic-write and recovery hardening while explicitly accepting Baileys’ production warning and fragmented Signal-key I/O.

recommendation.title: Shared database schema
recommendation.body: Add WhatsApp-owned Kysely tables to `state/openclaw.sqlite`, migrate transactionally, verify reopen, and remove legacy files only after a bounded backup period.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal spans the auth store, session boundary, and recent lifecycle refactors, making this the best available routing owner for the architecture choice.
